chapters.title: A Rebellious Nation Called to Account
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah opens with the Lord's lament that Judah, his own reared children, have rebelled against him while the ox knows its owner. Empty sacrifices cannot cover a corrupt nation, but the Lord invites them to reason together, promising that though their sins be as scarlet they may become white as snow.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Judah's rebellion against a loving father

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Empty sacrifice; come, let us reason together

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The faithful city becomes a harlot; redemption promised

chapters.title: The Mountain of the Lord's House
chapters.synopsis: In the last days the Lord's temple will be established above the mountains, and all nations will flow to it to learn his ways and beat their swords into plowshares. Isaiah then warns proud Judah, full of idols and treasure, that the haughtiness of men will be brought low in the day of the Lord alone.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Nations flow to the mountain of the Lord's house

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Pride and idols brought low in the day of the Lord

chapters.title: Judah's Leaders Fail the People
chapters.synopsis: The Lord removes Jerusalem's stay and staff, leaving the nation to be misruled by children and oppressed by extortioners while the poor are ground down. The proud daughters of Zion, decked in finery, are warned that their ornaments will turn to shame and their men will fall by the sword.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Leaders removed; the people oppressed

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The proud daughters of Zion humbled

chapters.title: A Branch Beautiful and Glorious
chapters.synopsis: After judgment thins their numbers, seven women will beg to be called by one man's name to take away their reproach. The Lord promises a branch that is beautiful and glorious, and a cloud of glory over Zion by day and a flaming fire by night, a covering and refuge for the remnant.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Seven women to one man after judgment

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The branch of the Lord and Zion's covering cloud

chapters.title: The Song of the Vineyard
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah sings of a well-tended vineyard that yields only wild grapes, a figure of Israel's failure despite the Lord's care, and pronounces woes upon those who join house to house, call evil good, and are mighty to drink wine. Because of this the Lord will lift an ensign to the nations, who come swiftly like a roaring lion.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The song of the unfruitful vineyard

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Six woes against Judah's corruption

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A distant nation summoned as the Lord's instrument

chapters.title: Isaiah's Vision and Call
chapters.synopsis: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up on his throne, attended by seraphim crying Holy, holy, holy. A live coal from the altar cleanses Isaiah's unclean lips, and when the Lord asks whom he shall send, Isaiah answers, Here am I; send me, and receives his commission despite a hard-hearted people.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord on his throne; seraphim cry holy

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The coal cleanses; Here am I, send me

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Isaiah's commission to a hardened people

chapters.title: The Sign of Immanuel
chapters.synopsis: When Syria and Israel threaten Jerusalem, the Lord sends Isaiah to reassure fearful King Ahaz that their plot will fail, and offers him a sign. Ahaz refuses to ask, so the Lord himself gives the sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel, God with us.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Ahaz reassured against the northern kings

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The sign of Immanuel offered and given

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Assyria to come as a scourge upon the land

chapters.title: Maher-shalal-hash-baz and a Sure Foundation
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah's son is named Maher-shalal-hash-baz as a sign that Damascus and Samaria will fall swiftly to Assyria, and the Lord warns Judah not to fear conspiracies but to sanctify him and make him their fear. Those who reject the gentle waters of Shiloah will be overwhelmed, and Isaiah binds up the testimony and seals the law among his disciples.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The sign-child; Assyria's swift overflow

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sanctify the Lord; seal the testimony among disciples

chapters.title: Unto Us a Child Is Born
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah promises that the people walking in darkness will see a great light, for unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace, upon whose government there will be no end. The chapter closes with warnings that pride and wickedness will bring the Lord's anger upon Israel and Syria.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The child born; government upon his shoulder

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Pride and wrath against Israel and Syria

chapters.title: Assyria, the Rod of the Lord's Anger
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah pronounces woe on unjust decree-makers and on Assyria, who though sent as the rod of the Lord's anger, boasts as if by his own power he cut off nations, and so will himself be punished. A remnant of Jacob will return and lean upon the Lord, and the Assyrian's yoke will be broken as in the day of Midian.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Assyria the rod, proud and to be punished

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A remnant returns; the Assyrian yoke broken

chapters.title: The Root of Jesse and Millennial Peace
chapters.synopsis: A rod comes forth out of the stem of Jesse, upon whom rests the spirit of the Lord, who judges the poor with righteousness and slays the wicked with the breath of his lips. Under his reign the wolf will dwell with the lamb and the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord, and he will gather scattered Israel a second time from the four corners of the earth.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The root of Jesse; wolf and lamb at peace

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Israel gathered a second time from all lands

chapters.title: A Song of Praise and Salvation
chapters.synopsis: In that day the redeemed will say the Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. They are told to draw water out of the wells of salvation with joy and to make known his deeds among the nations, for great is the Holy One of Israel in their midst.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A song of thanksgiving for salvation

chapters.title: The Burden of Babylon
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah lifts up an oracle against Babylon, calling for a gathering of nations as the Lord's battle-host to bring the great day of the Lord upon her, a day of terror and darkened heavens. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah, never inhabited again.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord's host mustered against Babylon

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Babylon overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah

chapters.title: Lucifer's Fall from Heaven
chapters.synopsis: The Lord promises to have mercy on Jacob and set Israel in their own land, giving them rest from sorrow and fear. Israel takes up a taunting proverb against the king of Babylon, likening his pride to Lucifer, son of the morning, who said in his heart I will be like the most High yet is brought down to the sides of the pit.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Mercy on Jacob; Israel restored to its land

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The taunt-song of Lucifer's fall

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Assyria's yoke broken; judgment on Philistia

chapters.title: The Burden of Moab
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah laments over Moab, whose cities are laid waste in a night and whose people flee weeping through the streets with shaven heads and sackcloth. The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and fugitives carry their grief as far as the brook of the willows.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Moab's cities wasted; the people flee in grief

chapters.title: Moab's Pride and Coming Ruin
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah calls Moab's fugitives to send tribute and find refuge under Zion's shadow, for Moab's pride and loud boasting will not save her. Within three years, as a hired servant counts, Moab's glory will be brought into contempt, and only a small remnant will remain.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Moab urged to seek refuge under Zion

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Moab's pride to end within three years

chapters.title: The Burden of Damascus
chapters.synopsis: Damascus is prophesied to cease being a city and become a ruinous heap, and the glory of Jacob's kingdom allied with her will fade like a forsaken forest. Because Israel has forgotten the God of her salvation, harvest will be scant, though at evening trouble the tumultuous nations that rush against her will vanish before morning.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Damascus to become a ruinous heap

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Israel's forgetfulness; rushing nations rebuked

chapters.title: A Message to the Land Beyond Ethiopia
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah addresses a distant, powerful land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, sending swift ambassadors, and describes the Lord watching quietly like clear heat before harvest until he cuts down the confident nations. In that day a people terrible from their beginning will bring a present to the Lord of hosts in Zion.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A distant land warned of coming harvest of judgment

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A present brought to the Lord in Zion

chapters.title: The Burden of Egypt
chapters.synopsis: The Lord rides upon a swift cloud into Egypt, and her idols tremble as civil strife, failed counsel, and a cruel lord bring her low. Yet the chapter turns to hope, promising an altar to the Lord in Egypt and a highway linking Egypt, Assyria, and Israel, a blessing in the midst of the earth.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Egypt's idols tremble; counsel and strength fail

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: An altar in Egypt; Egypt, Assyria, and Israel blessed together

chapters.title: Isaiah's Sign of Nakedness
chapters.synopsis: When Assyria's captain takes Ashdod, the Lord commands Isaiah to walk barefoot and stripped of his sackcloth for three years as a sign of the shame that will come upon Egypt and Ethiopia when Assyria leads them away captive. Those who trusted in Egypt for help are left to ask how they will escape.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Isaiah's sign of nakedness against Egypt's captors

chapters.title: The Fall of Babylon Foreseen
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah, distressed by a grievous vision, foresees the fall of Babylon to Elam and Media, and a watchman reports riders returning with word that Babylon has fallen, her graven gods broken to the ground. Shorter burdens against Dumah and Arabia follow, warning of fleeing tribes and Kedar's fading glory.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The watchman's report: Babylon is fallen

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Burdens of Dumah and Arabia

chapters.title: The Valley of Vision and a Faithful Steward
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah mourns over Jerusalem's careless revelry even as enemies breach her defenses, rebuking a people who eat and drink saying tomorrow we die instead of turning to the Lord. He then pronounces that Shebna the unfaithful steward will be removed and replaced by Eliakim, who will bear the key of the house of David.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Jerusalem's careless feasting amid the siege

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Shebna cast down; Eliakim given the key of David

chapters.title: The Burden of Tyre
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah pronounces judgment on Tyre, the merchant city whose traders were princes and whose fame reached the ends of the earth, now made to howl as her harbors fail. After seventy years the Lord will visit Tyre, and her hire will at last be consecrated holiness to the Lord.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Tyre's merchant glory brought to howling

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: After seventy years Tyre's gain consecrated to the Lord

chapters.title: The Earth Emptied and Judged
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah begins his little apocalypse, describing the earth utterly emptied and turned upside down because its inhabitants have transgressed laws and broken the everlasting covenant. Yet amid the desolation a remnant lifts up its voice in singing, for the Lord of hosts will reign gloriously in Zion before his ancients.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The earth emptied for its broken covenant

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A remnant sings; the Lord reigns in Zion

chapters.title: A Feast of Fat Things and Death Swallowed Up
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah praises the Lord for being a strength to the poor and a refuge from the storm, foreseeing a feast of fat things prepared for all people upon this mountain. There the Lord will swallow up death in victory, wipe away tears from all faces, and take away the reproach of his people from off all the earth.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Praise for the Lord as strength and refuge

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The feast of fat things; death swallowed up

chapters.title: A Song of Trust in Zion
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah gives a song for the strong city whose walls are salvation, where those who trust in the Lord are kept in perfect peace. He confesses that other lords besides the Lord have ruled over them, but promises the dead shall live, and their bodies shall arise as the earth casts out her dead.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A song of the strong city and perfect peace

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The dead shall live; hide until indignation passes

chapters.title: Leviathan Punished, Jacob Gathered
chapters.synopsis: In that day the Lord will punish leviathan the piercing serpent, and Israel will be like a vineyard the Lord keeps and waters continually rather than the fruitless vineyard of old. When Jacob's iniquity is purged, the Lord will thresh out his people from the Euphrates to the river of Egypt, and they will be gathered one by one to worship on the holy mountain.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Leviathan punished; the Lord's vineyard kept

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Jacob purged and gathered one by one

chapters.title: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah pronounces woe on the drunkards of Ephraim, whose fading crown of pride will be trodden down, and rebukes priests and prophets who err through strong drink and mock his teaching, precept upon precept. Yet the Lord lays in Zion a tried, precious cornerstone, and he that believeth shall not make haste, though he must also teach by strange judgment, as in threshing grain, that men may learn.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Ephraim's drunken pride; mockers of precept upon precept

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The precious cornerstone; wisdom in threshing

chapters.title: The Marvellous Work and a Wonder
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah warns Ariel, that is Jerusalem, that she will be brought low and speak as a familiar spirit out of the dust, her people's hearts far from the Lord though their lips honor him. He then foretells a marvellous work and a wonder in which a sealed book delivered to one unlearned, and a voice speaking as if from the dust, become a latter-day sign fulfilled in the coming forth of the Book of Mormon, restoring understanding to those whose eyes and ears have been closed.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Ariel humbled; lip-service without the heart

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The sealed book and voice from the dust, sign of the Book of Mormon

chapters.title: Woe to Those Who Trust in Egypt
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah condemns rebellious children who seek help from Egypt without asking the Lord, calling them a rebellious people who bid the seers not to see. Yet the Lord waits to be gracious, promising that though bread and water be scant, their Teacher will not be removed, and their ears will hear a word behind them saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Trust in Egypt rebuked as rebellion

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord waits to be gracious; a voice behind them guides

chapters.title: Woe to Those Who Trust in Horses
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah warns against relying on Egypt's horses and chariots instead of looking to the Holy One of Israel, for the Egyptians are men and not God, and their help shall fail. The Lord of hosts will defend Jerusalem as birds hovering, and Assyria will fall by a sword not of man.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Woe to those trusting Egypt's horses

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord defends Jerusalem; Assyria falls

chapters.title: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah foresees a king who reigns in righteousness and princes who rule in judgment, each a hiding place from the wind, until the Spirit is poured from on high and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field. He warns the careless women of complacent ease that briers and thorns will overtake the land before that peace comes.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A righteous king and princes of judgment

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Careless women warned of coming desolation

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Spirit poured out; peace and quiet resting places

chapters.title: Woe to the Spoiler; Zion's King Beheld
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah pronounces woe upon the spoiler who has not himself been spoiled, and the people cry to the Lord to be gracious in trouble, as the land mourns under a treacherous foe. Sinners in Zion are afraid, but those who walk righteously will dwell on high and behold the King in his beauty in a land of far distances made near.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Woe to the treacherous spoiler

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The righteous behold the King in his beauty

chapters.title: The Lord's Vengeance on the Nations
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah summons all nations to hear of the Lord's indignation against them, when the heavens are rolled together as a scroll and his sword comes down upon Edom in judgment. The land becomes burning pitch and brimstone, possessed forever by wild creatures, for the Lord has cast the lot for it.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord's day of vengeance upon Edom and the nations

chapters.title: The Desert Shall Blossom as the Rose
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah promises that the wilderness and the solitary place will be glad and the desert will rejoice and blossom as the rose, with the eyes of the blind opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. A highway called the way of holiness will be raised up, and the ransomed of the Lord will return to Zion with everlasting joy upon their heads.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The desert blossoms; blind eyes and deaf ears opened

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The highway of holiness; the ransomed return with joy

chapters.title: Sennacherib Threatens Jerusalem
chapters.synopsis: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year, Assyria's king Sennacherib besieges Judah's fortified cities, and his commander Rabshakeh stands before Jerusalem's wall to mock Hezekiah's trust in Egypt and in the Lord, urging the people to surrender. Hezekiah's officials ask him to speak in Aramaic, but he deliberately speaks in Hebrew to frighten the people on the wall.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Sennacherib's forces besiege Judah

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Rabshakeh mocks Hezekiah before the wall

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Angel's Deliverance
chapters.synopsis: Hezekiah rends his clothes and sends to Isaiah, who assures him the Lord will defend Jerusalem, and when Sennacherib sends a taunting letter, Hezekiah spreads it before the Lord in the temple and prays. The Lord answers through Isaiah that the Assyrian will not enter the city, and that night the angel of the Lord slays the Assyrian camp, so Sennacherib withdraws and is later slain by his own sons.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Hezekiah seeks Isaiah amid the threat

segments.speaker: hezekiah
segments.note: Hezekiah's prayer in the temple

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The angel destroys the Assyrian camp

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Illness and the Sundial Sign
chapters.synopsis: Hezekiah falls sick unto death, and after his earnest weeping prayer the Lord adds fifteen years to his life, giving the shadow's retreat on the sundial as a sign. Hezekiah writes a psalm of thanksgiving for his recovery from the pit of corruption.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Hezekiah's prayer; fifteen years added; the sundial sign

segments.speaker: hezekiah
segments.note: Hezekiah's psalm of recovery

chapters.title: Envoys from Babylon
chapters.synopsis: Babylon's king sends envoys with gifts to Hezekiah after his illness, and Hezekiah proudly shows them all his treasures and armory. Isaiah then prophesies that everything in the house will one day be carried away to Babylon and that some of Hezekiah's own sons will become eunuchs in that foreign court.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Babylon's envoys shown Hezekiah's treasures

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Prophecy of the Babylonian captivity to come

chapters.title: Comfort Ye My People
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah opens the book of comfort with the Lord's tender charge to speak comfortably to Jerusalem, for her warfare is accomplished, and a voice cries to prepare the way of the Lord in the wilderness. All flesh is grass that withers, but the word of the Lord stands forever, and those who wait upon him will renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Comfort ye my people; the voice in the wilderness

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord's incomparable greatness over creation

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Those who wait on the Lord renew their strength

chapters.title: Fear Not, I Will Help Thee
chapters.synopsis: The Lord calls the nations to judgment, asking who raised up the one from the east who tramples kings, while reassuring Israel his servant, chosen and not cast away, saying fear thou not, for I am with thee. He promises to make the poor and needy find water in the desert, so that all may see and know the hand of the Lord has done this.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Fear not, for I am with thee

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Idols challenged to foretell things to come

chapters.title: The Lord's Chosen Servant
chapters.synopsis: The Lord presents his servant, in whom his soul delights, who will bring forth judgment gently to the Gentiles, not crying nor breaking a bruised reed, and be given as a light to open blind eyes and free prisoners from darkness. He declares he will do a new thing and sing a new song, yet rebukes Israel, blind and deaf though chosen, for not laying these things to heart.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The gentle servant, a light to the Gentiles

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A new song; the Lord marches to battle

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Israel blind and deaf despite being chosen

chapters.title: Fear Not, for I Have Redeemed Thee
chapters.synopsis: The Lord reassures Israel that having created and redeemed her by name, she is precious in his sight, and he will gather her seed from east and west, north and south. He declares himself the only Savior, blots out Israel's transgressions for his own sake, and promises to do a new thing, making a way in the wilderness for his chosen people.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Fear not; Israel gathered from every direction

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A new way made in the wilderness

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Israel's neglect; transgressions blotted out

chapters.title: None Beside the Lord; Idols Mocked
chapters.synopsis: The Lord pours his spirit upon Israel's seed like water on thirsty ground, declaring himself the first and the last, beside whom there is no God. He mocks the folly of the idol-maker who burns half a tree for warmth and bows to the other half as a god, then names Cyrus as his shepherd who will fulfill his pleasure in rebuilding Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The spirit poured out; there is no other God

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The folly of the idol-maker

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Cyrus named as the Lord's shepherd

chapters.title: Cyrus, the Lord's Anointed
chapters.synopsis: The Lord calls Cyrus his anointed, whose right hand he holds to subdue nations, though Cyrus does not know him, that all may know there is none beside the Lord who forms light and creates darkness. He invites all the ends of the earth to look unto him and be saved, for every knee shall bow and every tongue confess.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Cyrus raised up though he knows not the Lord

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Look unto me and be saved, all the earth

chapters.title: Babylon's Idols Bow, the Lord Carries
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah contrasts Babylon's gods Bel and Nebo, carried as burdens on beasts into captivity, with the Lord who has carried Israel from the womb and will still carry and deliver them in old age. He declares the end from the beginning, calling a ravenous bird, meaning Cyrus, from the east to fulfill his counsel.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Bel and Nebo carried away as helpless burdens

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord who carries Israel declares the end from the beginning

chapters.title: The Fall of the Virgin Daughter of Babylon
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah pronounces Babylon's humiliation, calling her the tender and delicate one to sit in the dust, for she trusted in her wickedness and said none seeth me. Her sorceries and many enchantments will not save her, and evil will come upon her suddenly which she cannot charm away.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Babylon's pride and sorceries brought to sudden ruin

chapters.title: Refined in the Furnace of Affliction
chapters.synopsis: The Lord rebukes Israel for swearing by his name without truth or righteousness, yet declares he has refined her in the furnace of affliction for his own name's sake and will not give his glory to another. He urges them to go forth from Babylon, proclaiming that the Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob, though there is no peace to the wicked.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Israel refined in the furnace for the Lord's name

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Go forth from Babylon; no peace to the wicked

chapters.title: A Light to the Gentiles; Can a Mother Forget
chapters.synopsis: The Lord's servant is called from the womb to be a light to the Gentiles and to bring Jacob again to him, and though Zion says the Lord has forsaken her, he answers that a mother might forget her child, yet he will not forget her, for her walls are graven upon his hands. Kings and queens will become nursing fathers and mothers to Israel, gathered from far countries.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The servant called as a light to the Gentiles

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Can a mother forget her child? Zion never forgotten

chapters.title: The Servant's Obedience in Suffering
chapters.synopsis: The Lord asks where Israel's mother was put away for, having only their own sins as the cause of separation, and his servant declares he gave his back to the smiters and his cheeks to those who plucked off the hair, not hiding his face from shame because the Lord God helps him. He calls those who fear the Lord to trust in his name even while walking in darkness.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Israel's separation caused by her own sins

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The servant's obedience through suffering

chapters.title: Look unto Abraham; Awake, O Arm of the Lord
chapters.synopsis: The Lord bids the righteous look to the rock from which they were hewn, to Abraham and Sarah, and promises that the Lord will comfort Zion and make her wilderness like Eden. He calls on his own arm to awake as in the days of old that dried up the sea, and promises the ransomed of the Lord shall return with everlasting joy.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Look unto Abraham and Sarah, the rock hewn

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Awake, O arm of the Lord, as in days of old

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Awake, Jerusalem, the cup of trembling removed

chapters.title: Awake, Awake, O Zion
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah calls Zion to put on her beautiful garments, for the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter her, and celebrates how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings of peace. The chapter closes as the Lord's servant is exalted and extolled, though many will be astonished at his marred appearance beyond that of any man.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Awake, Zion; beautiful are the feet of the messenger

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The servant exalted though marred beyond recognition

chapters.title: He Was Wounded for Our Transgressions
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah's suffering-servant song describes one despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows acquainted with grief, who was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities, bearing the chastisement of our peace. Though he is led as a lamb to the slaughter and cut off from the land of the living, the Lord will prolong his days and he will see the travail of his soul and be satisfied.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: A man of sorrows wounded for our transgressions

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Led as a lamb to the slaughter; the Lord's pleasure prospers

chapters.title: Zion's Everlasting Covenant of Peace
chapters.synopsis: The Lord calls the barren woman to sing, for her seed will inherit the Gentiles and her desolate cities be inhabited, since her Maker is her husband, the Lord of hosts. Though he hid his face a moment, with everlasting kindness he gathers her, and swears as in the days of Noah never again to be wroth, promising a covenant of peace no weapon formed against her shall prosper.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The barren woman sings; everlasting kindness restored

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: No weapon formed against thee shall prosper

chapters.title: Come to the Waters
chapters.synopsis: The Lord invites everyone who thirsts to come to the waters freely, to buy wine and milk without money and without price, and to incline their ear that their soul may live through an everlasting covenant. He assures that his thoughts are higher than our thoughts, and his word that goes forth will not return void but accomplish what he pleases.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Come, buy wine and milk without price

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord's word accomplishes what it is sent to do

chapters.title: Strangers and Eunuchs Welcomed
chapters.synopsis: The Lord promises that the stranger and the eunuch who join themselves to him and keep his covenant will have a place and a name within his house, better than sons and daughters, for his house will be called a house of prayer for all people. He rebukes Israel's blind watchmen, greedy dogs that cannot bark, who look only to their own gain.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A house of prayer for all people, strangers included

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Israel's blind and greedy watchmen rebuked

chapters.title: The Righteous Perish, Idolatry Rebuked
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah observes that the righteous perish and no one lays it to heart, taken away from evil to come, while he rebukes Israel's idolatry under every green tree and their forsaking of the Lord for false gods. Yet the Lord who inhabits eternity dwells also with the humble and contrite, promising peace to him that is near and to him that is far off.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The righteous taken from evil; idolatry rebuked

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord dwells with the humble and contrite

chapters.title: The True Fast the Lord Has Chosen
chapters.synopsis: The Lord rebukes a people who fast for show while oppressing their laborers and quarreling, and defines the fast he has chosen: to loose the bands of wickedness, to feed the hungry, and to bring the homeless poor into one's house. If they honor the sabbath and remove the yoke, their light will break forth as the morning and they will be called repairers of the breach.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Empty fasting for show is rebuked

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The true fast: loose bonds, feed the hungry, honor the sabbath

chapters.title: Sins That Separate from God
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah declares that the Lord's hand is not shortened, but iniquities have separated the people from their God, whose hands are stained with blood and whose feet run to evil. Seeing no one to intercede, the Lord himself brings salvation with his own arm, and a Redeemer will come to Zion for those who turn from transgression.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Iniquities have separated Israel from God

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Lord's own arm brings salvation; a Redeemer comes to Zion

chapters.title: Arise, Shine, for Thy Light Is Come
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah calls Zion to arise and shine, for her light has come and the glory of the Lord is risen upon her, and Gentiles and kings will come to her light bringing gold and incense. Her gates will stay open continually to receive the wealth of nations, the sun and moon will be surpassed by the Lord's own glory, and violence will no longer be heard in her land.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Arise, shine; nations come to Zion's light

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Violence ends; the Lord himself is Zion's everlasting light

chapters.title: The Spirit of the Lord God Is upon Me
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah's servant declares the Spirit of the Lord God is upon him, anointed to preach good tidings to the meek, to bind up the brokenhearted, and to proclaim liberty to captives and the acceptable year of the Lord, words Jesus later reads and applies to himself. Those who mourn in Zion will be given beauty for ashes and be called trees of righteousness, and the Lord promises to clothe his people with garments of salvation.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The Spirit of the Lord upon the anointed servant

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Beauty for ashes; garments of salvation

chapters.title: Zion's New Name and Coming Glory
chapters.synopsis: For Zion's sake Isaiah will not hold his peace until her righteousness goes forth as brightness, and she is given a new name and called Hephzibah and Beulah, for the Lord delights in her as a bridegroom in his bride. Watchmen are set upon her walls to give the Lord no rest until Jerusalem is established, and the redeemed are called the sought out, a city not forsaken.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Zion's new name; the Lord delights in her as a bride

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Watchmen on the walls; Zion the sought out

chapters.title: Who Is This That Cometh from Edom
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah beholds a mighty figure coming from Edom with garments stained red, who declares he has trodden the winepress of wrath alone, for the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come. Isaiah then recalls the Lord's lovingkindnesses to Israel of old and pleads for the Lord to look down from heaven upon his afflicted people.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: The mighty one from Edom, garments stained in judgment

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Recalling the Lord's mercies; a plea for his people

chapters.title: Oh That Thou Wouldest Rend the Heavens
chapters.synopsis: Isaiah cries for the Lord to rend the heavens and come down as at Sinai, that the nations may tremble at his presence, confessing that all their righteousnesses are as filthy rags before him. He pleads as with a potter, calling Israel the clay and the Lord the potter, the work of his hand, and asks him not to be wroth beyond measure with a desolate Zion.

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens and come down

segments.speaker: isaiah
segments.note: We are the clay, thou the potter; be not wroth

chapters.title: New Heavens and a New Earth
chapters.synopsis: The Lord answers that he is sought of those who did not ask for him, while a rebellious people who sacrifice in gardens and eat swine's flesh provoke him continually, so that judgment falls yet a remnant, his elect, is preserved for blessing. He promises to create new heavens and a new earth in which the former troubles are forgotten, the child will not die a hundred years old, and the wolf and the lamb will feed together.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A rebellious people judged; the elect preserved

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: New heavens and a new earth of peace

chapters.title: Heaven Is My Throne, Earth My Footstool
chapters.synopsis: The Lord declares that heaven is his throne and earth his footstool, and that he looks to the man who is poor and of a contrite spirit and trembles at his word, rather than to empty temple ritual offered by hypocrites. He promises Zion will bring forth her children as in a moment, comforting them like a mother, while gathering all nations to see his glory and pronouncing lasting judgment on the rebellious.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The contrite honored above empty ritual

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Zion's children born in a moment; comfort like a mother

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Nations gathered to see the Lord's glory; judgment endures
